plain: Livecoins reports crypto custodian Zodia Custody, a Standard Chartered subsidiary, confirmed a client data leak. Business contact names and email addresses of a small part of clients and employees were exposed.

sources.name: Livecoins: Standard Chartered's crypto custody firm confirms client data leak
Bloomingbit: SC 산하 조디아커스터디서 보안 사고…고객 정보 유출 (relaying Reuters)
GBHackers (relaying Reuters): Zodia Custody hit by data breach

summary: Livecoins reports that Zodia Custody, a Standard Chartered subsidiary, confirmed a client data breach and took its B2B API offline as a precaution. CEO Richard Clark said it detected attempts to probe its platform on 23 November. According to Livecoins, a small part of clients and employees had business contact names and email addresses leaked; no number was given. GBHackers, relaying Reuters, says Clark reported no unauthorized transactions so far.
title: Zodia Custody, Standard Chartered's crypto custody arm, confirms leak of client business contact data, Livecoins reports

validation.note: Verify desk: Livecoins and Bloomingbit (relaying Reuters) independently report that Zodia CEO Richard Clark said a breach exposing some customer and employee data was detected on 23 November. The contact-detail scope and API shutdown rest on Livecoins only; Zodia's own statement not read.

review.note: Compared title, 23 Nov probing quote, API offline, contact names/emails, no count, no unauthorized transactions against Livecoins and GBHackers
